name: Deception Pass Bridge Overlook
highlight: Two green steel spans stitch Whidbey to Fidalgo about 180 feet above a tidal channel that runs like a river. Walk the bluff on the north side and you get madronas leaning over the rock, the current pulling standing waves through the gap, and the San Juans stacked up behind it.

name: Kerry Park
highlight: A single stone terrace on the south slope of Queen Anne, with the Space Needle at roughly eye level and the downtown towers stacked behind it. On a clear evening Mount Rainier sits above the skyline; it is one small wall, so you will be sharing it.

name: Peshastin Pinnacles
highlight: Sandstone fins tilt out of the orchard floor like the plates of something buried. Short, steep paths put you on a bench of bare rock with pear and apple rows below and the Wenatchee River valley opening east.

name: Palouse Falls Overlook
highlight: The Palouse River drops about 200 feet into a round basalt bowl, then knifes off through a columnar gorge. Three fenced viewpoints look straight across at it; the upper Fryxell Overlook gives you the falls and the whole scoured canyon in one frame.

name: Ecola Point
highlight: The entrance road climbs through Sitka spruce and then opens onto a grass bluff over the Pacific. Look south and you get the whole run of shoreline with sea stacks punctuating it, Cannon Beach at the far end and the coast range behind.

name: North Head Lighthouse Overlook, Cape Disappointment
highlight: A white 1898 tower on a cliff at the mouth of the Columbia, with the Pacific on three sides and the Long Beach Peninsula running north. The overlook is a small railed shelf — wind is the whole character of the place.

name: Smith Rock State Park
highlight: Welded tuff walls the color of apricot stand several hundred feet over a bend in the Crooked River. The Misery Ridge trail tops out with Monkey Face on one side and the Cascade volcanoes lined up white on the horizon.

fact.verbatim: Smith Rock State Park is a popular location for wedding, engagement, senior and family photoshoots. name: International Rose Test Garden, Washington Park
highlight: Terraced beds of test roses step down the west hills in tight rows, with a gazebo on the lower tier and the city below the tree line. Peak bloom turns the whole slope into blocks of color.

highlight: An octagonal stone rotunda from 1918 set on a promontory 693 feet above the Columbia, with marble floors and stained glass inside. From the parapet the river bends away east between the Gorge walls.
